samples.summary: Spawn-time `error` may still crash the CLI: the ordering claim the new comment relies on is unverified for `open`'s default `wait: false` path
samples.evidence: The delta's new comment (test/login-callback.test.ts:172-177) and the helper doc (src/commands/login.ts:101-113) both rest on the claim that `open` v11 attaches `once('error', reject)` in the same synchronous turn as `spawn()` ("index.js: spawn at :255, listener at :301, no await between them"), so a missing-opener ENOENT surfaces as a rejection caught by the `try` at login.ts:119. In every `open` release I can recall (v8-v10) that `once('error', reject)` lives **only inside the `if (options.wait)` branch**; with the default `wait: false` (which is what `openBrowser` uses — `open(url)` with no options, login.ts:121) `baseOpen` does `subprocess.unref(); return subprocess;` with no error listener at all. If that is still true in v11, the ENOENT that `child_process.spawn` schedules on `process.nextTick` is emitted onto an emitter with no `error` listener, and the nextTick queue drains before our promise continuation, so `child?.on?.('error', ...)` at login.ts:122 is attached too late — the unhandled `error` event becomes an uncaughtException and takes the CLI down mid-login on exactly the headless boxes this helper exists to survive. I could not confirm either way: `node_modules` is not present in the tree (pnpm-lock.yaml:7756 pins `open@11.0.0`), so the cited line numbers :255/:301 are unverifiable from the repo, and neither test exercises the real ordering — one mocks a resolved child and emits synchronously afterwards (test:187-196), the other mocks a rejection (test:198-204), so both pass regardless of which branch `open` actually takes. Someone should read node_modules/open/index.js and, if the listener is inside the `wait` branch, either pass `{wait: true}`-equivalent handling or attach the `error` handler via a wrapper that owns the spawn.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: `openBrowser` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:118-126) attaches `child?.on?.('error', ...)` only after `await open(url)`, and both the helper doc (login.ts:92-117) and the test comment (test/login-callback.test.ts:168-181) rest on the unverified claim that `open` v11 attaches `once('error', reject)` synchronously with the spawn on the default `wait: false` path. I could not verify that claim from this repository: node_modules is absent (no `**/node_modules/open/index.js`, no vendored copy, no patch — grep for `baseOpen`/`subprocess.unref`/`once('spawn'` returns nothing), and packages/cli/package.json:28 pins only `^11.0.0`. In `open` v8-v10 the `once('error', reject)` lives inside the `if (options.wait)` branch only, so a spawn ENOENT would be emitted on the nextTick queue onto a listener-less ChildProcess before the post-`await` continuation runs. Nothing mitigates that here: the path is live (login.ts:285 default dep, login.ts:351 call site) and there is no `process.on('uncaughtException')`/`unhandledRejection` handler anywhere under packages/cli/src, so the unhandled `error` event would take the CLI down mid-login on headless machines. The two openBrowser tests mock a resolved EventEmitter (test:187-196) and a rejected promise (test:198-204), so neither exercises the real ordering. No refutation ground applies — the code is not absent, not guarded elsewhere, and an unguarded crash path is in the correctness lane. Confidence is low because the underlying `open` v11 behavior is unverifiable in-tree, which is exactly why the finding must be kept.
